headline: Thursday's Rout: Chips Crater as Nearly Every Stock Falls
body_html:
Thursday's session was a rout, not a rotation in the usual sense. Of the 524 stocks in our universe, only 45 rose and 477 fell. The Nasdaq slipped into correction territory, the market's fear gauge jumped by the most since April, and retail traders reportedly shed more stocks in a single day than at any point since the Covid sell-off.

Every sector we track closed lower, but the damage was uneven. Semiconductors fell nearly 12%, far worse than industrials at 4.74%, energy and materials at 4.22% each, and consumer at 3.9%. Software gave up 2.99% and healthcare 2.15%. Homebuilders held up best, down 1.16%. Memory maker Sandisk lost 22.26% and MaxLinear 22.06%, which kept the chip group at the center of the selling.

The few winners were mostly in healthcare. ADMA Biologics climbed 26.05%, and IT services firm EPAM Systems rose 20.63%. When this few stocks rise, the day is about forced selling and risk reduction, not company news. Friday will show whether buyers return or the pressure carries over.

briefs.headline: Nasdaq Enters Correction, Erasing the Election Bounce
briefs.body: The Nasdaq's slide into correction territory wiped out the rally that followed the election. Commentators are already asking what usually comes next after such a drop. Thursday's reading, with 477 of 524 tracked stocks lower, offered little sign of a quick answer.

briefs.headline: Fear Gauge Jumps, and Some Say It Should Go Higher
briefs.body: Wall Street's volatility index posted its biggest one-day surge since April. Some traders argue that, given the speed of the equity decline, it should be even higher. That suggests investors are still not fully pricing in further turbulence.

briefs.headline: Retail Investors Sell in Bulk
briefs.body: Individual traders unloaded more stocks in a single session than on any day since the Covid sell-off, according to market reports. Heavy retail selling often shows up in the most speculative corners, and Thursday's steep losses in chips and consumer names fit that picture.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Tankers and an Iranian Proposal Keep Gulf in Focus
briefs.body: Tankers were reportedly hit in the Strait of Hormuz as Iran kept up pressure after the US vote. Separately, an Iranian official said a nuclear proposal had gone to Washington through Qatar. Mixed signals from the region added to an already nervous tape.

briefs.headline: Bank of England Hikes for the First Time Since 2023
briefs.body: The Bank of England raised interest rates for the first time in about two years and warned that more increases are likely. The move reminded investors that policy is tightening abroad, which weighs on risk appetite when equities are already under strain.

briefs.headline: Energy Slips Even as an Oil Major Lifts Its Payout
briefs.body: ConocoPhillips raised its dividend after earnings beat estimates on higher oil prices. Yet our energy group still fell 4.22%, in line with materials. Thursday's selling hit even sectors with supportive fundamentals, and strong results offered little shelter.
